title: SSC CHSL (10+2) Tier-I — Full-Length CBT Mock Paper
subtitle: 100 Questions • 60 Minutes • 200 Marks • Official +2 / -0.50 Marking
description: Exact full-length SSC Combined Higher Secondary Level (10+2) Tier-I CBT replica modelled on 2023–2024 Tier-I papers: 100 objective MCQs across English Language (25), General Intelligence (25), Quantitative Aptitude (25), and General Awareness (25) in 60 minutes.
instructions: Exact SSC CHSL (10+2) Tier-I pattern: 4 sections × 25 questions = 100 questions (200 maximum marks) in 60 minutes.
Official marking scheme: +2 marks for each correct answer, -0.50 marks penalty for each wrong answer, and 0 for unattempted questions.
Free navigation across all four sections is enabled throughout the 60-minute composite duration.

chsl_cloze_1.title: Cloze Test — Questions 21 to 25 (English Language)
chsl_cloze_1.content:
Read the following passage carefully and choose the most appropriate word for each blank.

Public libraries have long served as democratic pillars of lifelong learning. In an era dominated by short-form digital feeds, quiet reading halls __(1)__ students and citizens a rare sanctuary for deep concentration. Modern community libraries are no longer __(2)__ to dusty bookshelves; they now provide high-speed internet terminals, competitive exam archives, and Braille collections for __(3)__ readers. By investing steadily __(4)__ neighbourhood libraries, state governments can bridge educational divides and nurture an __(5)__ electorate.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate SYNONYM of the given word: `PRUDENT`
questions.explanation: 'Prudent' means acting with or showing care and thought for the future; wise and judicious.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word: `ABUNDANT`
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing in large quantities; its antonym is 'Scarce'.

questions.question:
Select the one-word substitute for:
`A life history of a person written by that person himself`
questions.explanation: An 'Autobiography' is a self-written account of one's own life.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom:
`Once in a blue moon`
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' means something that happens very rarely.

questions.question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error:
`She is senior / than me / by three years / in this department.`
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives like senior, junior, superior, inferior, and prior take 'to', not 'than': `senior to me`.

questions.question: The suspect was acquitted ______ all charges due to lack of credible evidence.
questions.explanation: The standard legal collocation is `acquitted of` charges.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is `Millennium` (double 'l' and double 'n').

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form:
`Did the postman deliver the registered parcel yesterday?`
options: Was the registered parcel delivered by the postman yesterday?
Were the registered parcel delivered by the postman yesterday?
Has the registered parcel been delivered by the postman yesterday?
Is the registered parcel delivered by the postman yesterday?
questions.explanation: Simple Past Interrogative (`Did + S + V1`) becomes `Was/Were + O + V3` in Passive voice.

questions.question:
Convert into indirect speech:
`Ramesh said, "I am preparing for the CHSL examination."`
options: Ramesh said that he is preparing for the CHSL examination.
Ramesh said that he was preparing for the CHSL examination.
Ramesh told that I was preparing for the CHSL examination.
Ramesh said that he had been preparing for the CHSL examination.
questions.explanation: Reporting verb in past tense shifts Present Continuous (`am preparing`) to Past Continuous (`was preparing`).

questions.question:
Improve the bracketed part:
`No sooner did the bell ring (when) the students rushed out of the hall.`
questions.explanation: `No sooner` is always followed by `than`.

questions.question:
Select the meaning of the idiom:
`Spill the beans`
options: To make a mess in the kitchen
questions.explanation: 'Spill the beans' means to disclose secret or confidential information unintentionally or prematurely.

questions.question:
Select the one-word substitute for:
`A place where birds are kept`
questions.explanation: An `Aviary` is a large enclosure for keeping birds (whereas an `Apiary` is for bees).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate SYNONYM of: `CANDID`
questions.explanation: 'Candid' means truthful, straightforward, and frank.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of: `OPTIMISTIC`
questions.explanation: The direct opposite of 'Optimistic' (hopeful) is 'Pessimistic' (expecting the worst).

questions.question:
Identify the segment with a grammatical error:
`One of my closest friend / has been selected / for the national / scholarship programme.`
questions.explanation: `One of + plural noun` is required: `One of my closest friends`.

questions.question:
Rearrange the segments to form a meaningful sentence:
P. of solar micro-grids
Q. has transformed rural
R. the rapid deployment
S. livelihoods across India
questions.explanation: 'The rapid deployment (R) of solar micro-grids (P) has transformed rural (Q) livelihoods across India (S).'

questions.question: Despite facing severe financial ______, the young inventor completed her prototype on schedule.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' introduces a contrast, so 'financial constraints' (limitations) fits logically.

questions.question: Select the CORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: `Surveillance` (sur + veil + lance) is the correct spelling.

questions.question:
Substitute the bracketed segment:
`If I (was) you, I would accept the transfer order immediately.`
questions.explanation: Hypothetical/subjunctive conditional sentences use `were` for all subjects: `If I were you`.

questions.question:
Select the passive form of the imperative sentence:
`Switch off the fans before leaving.`
options: Let the fans be switched off before leaving.
The fans are switched off before leaving.
Let the fans switched off before leaving.
You were told to switch off the fans before leaving.
questions.explanation: Imperative sentences follow `Let + object + be + V3`: `Let the fans be switched off before leaving.`

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (1).
questions.explanation: Quiet reading halls 'offer' students and citizens a sanctuary for deep concentration.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (2).
questions.explanation: 'No longer confined to dusty bookshelves' means not limited solely to print books.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (3).
questions.explanation: Braille collections specifically serve 'visually impaired' readers.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (4).
questions.explanation: The verb 'invest' takes the preposition 'in' (`investing steadily in neighbourhood libraries`).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (5).
questions.explanation: Libraries nurture an 'informed' electorate.

questions.question: `Ammeter : Electric Current :: Barometer : ?`
questions.explanation: An Ammeter measures electric current; a Barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.question:
Find the next term in the series:
`4, 9, 19, 39, 79, ?`
questions.explanation: Each term follows $2n + 1$: $79 \times 2 + 1 = 159$.

questions.question: In a certain code language, `DELHI` is written as `CCIDD`. How is `BOMBAY` written in that code?
questions.explanation: Letters shift backward by -1, -2, -3, -4, -5, -6: B-1=A, O-2=M, M-3=J, B-4=X, A-5=V, Y-6=S ⇒ `AMJXVS`.

questions.question: Three of the following four numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one out.
questions.explanation: $121 = 11^2$, $169 = 13^2$, $225 = 15^2$ are perfect squares; $243 = 3^5$ is not a perfect square.

questions.question: A is the brother of B. B is the daughter of C. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: A and B are children of C, and D is C's father. Since A is male (brother of B), A is D's Grandson.

questions.question: Meera walks 6 km East, then turns left and walks 8 km. What is the shortest straight-line distance from her starting point?
questions.explanation: Right triangle with legs 6 km and 8 km: $\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = 10\text{ km}$.

questions.question:
If `A` denotes `+`, `B` denotes `×`, `C` denotes `-`, and `D` denotes `÷`, find the value of:
`72 D 9 B 4 A 15 C 11`

Statements:
1. All apples are fruits.
2. All fruits are sweet.

Conclusions:
I. All apples are sweet.
II. Some sweet things are apples.
questions.explanation: Apples ⊂ Fruits ⊂ Sweet ⇒ All apples are sweet (I) and its valid conversion Some sweet things are apples (II) both follow.

questions.question:
Complete the series:
`AZ, CX, EV, GT, ?`
questions.explanation: First letter +2 (A,C,E,G,I) and second letter -2 (Z,X,V,T,R), forming opposite pairs ⇒ `IR`.
Logic: $n : n(n+1)$. Check: $14 \times 15 = 210$. So $18 \times 19 = 342$.

questions.question: In a queue, Neha is 12th from the front and Priya is 15th from the back. If there are 4 persons standing between them (and Neha is ahead of Priya), how many persons are in the queue?
questions.explanation: Non-overlapping total = $12 + 4 + 15 = 31$ persons.

questions.question: What is the acute angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:30?
If a wall clock shows 4:20, what time will appear in its vertical mirror reflection?
If `KING` is coded as `PRMT` using reverse-alphabet pairs (A↔Z, B↔Y), how is `QUEEN` coded?
Which relationship best represents: `Asia`, `India`, and `New Delhi`?
options: Three concentric circles (New Delhi inside India inside Asia)
Two circles inside a third separate circle
questions.explanation: New Delhi is completely inside India, and India is completely inside Asia (concentric nested circles).

questions.question:
Find the missing number in the sequence:
`3, 7, 16, 35, 74, ?`
questions.explanation: Pattern: $\times 2 + 1, \times 2 + 2, \times 2 + 3, \times 2 + 4, \times 2 + 5$: $74 \times 2 + 5 = 153$.

questions.question: Which of the following words CANNOT be formed using the letters of `ENVIRONMENT` (each letter used at most as many times as it appears)?
questions.explanation: `ENVIRONMENT` contains only one `M`, whereas `MOVEMENT` requires two `M`s.

questions.question:
Which word will appear THIRD if arranged in English dictionary order?
1. Monitor  2. Monkey  3. Monologue  4. Monument  5. Monarch
questions.explanation: Order: Monarch (1) → Monitor (2) → Monkey (3) → Monologue (4) → Monument (5). Third word is `Monkey`.

questions.question: In an unfolded standard cube net where face `1` is adjacent to `2, 3, 4, 5` in a cross shape and `6` is attached to `2`, which face is opposite to `1`?
questions.explanation: Since `1` is adjacent to all four faces `2, 3, 4, 5`, the only remaining face `6` must lie opposite to `1`.

questions.question: Select the set related in the same way as `(5, 12, 13)` and `(8, 15, 17)`:
The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 54 years. Six years ago, the father was twice as old as his son. What is the son's present age?
questions.explanation: 6 years ago, sum = $54 - 12 = 42$. Ratio $2:1 \Rightarrow$ son was $42/3 = 14$. Present age = $14 + 6 = 20$ years.

questions.question: Select the odd word out from the given alternatives.
questions.explanation: Sitar, Violin, and Guitar are stringed instruments; Flute is a wind instrument.

questions.question: Which of the following years is NOT a leap year?
questions.explanation: Century years must be divisible by 400 to be leap years. 1900 is not divisible by 400, so it is an ordinary year.

questions.question:
Statements:
1. Some books are novels.
2. All novels are stories.

Conclusions:
I. Some books are stories.
II. All stories are novels.
questions.explanation: Since some books are novels and all novels are stories, those books are stories (I follows). II does not follow.

questions.question:
Arrange in a meaningful logical order:
1. Seed  2. Plant  3. Fruit  4. Tree  5. Flower
questions.explanation: Biological growth order: Seed (1) → Plant (2) → Tree (4) → Flower (5) → Fruit (3).

questions.question: Evaluate: $25 \times 16 \div 8 + 14 - 9$
In an examination, a student scored 32% marks and failed by 24 marks. Another student scored 40% marks and got 16 marks above the pass mark. Find the maximum marks.
By selling an article for ₹720, a trader loses 10%. At what price should he sell it to gain 15%?
Find the simple interest on ₹6,400 at $7.5\%$ per annum for 4 years.
A sum of ₹8,000 is invested at 5% per annum compounded annually. What will be the compound interest after 2 years?
Divide ₹1,560 among A, B, and C in the ratio $3 : 4 : 5$. What is C's share?
questions.explanation: Sum of parts = $3+4+5=12$. C's share = $\frac{5}{12} \times 1560 = 5 \times 130 = ₹650$.

questions.question: Find the average of the first 25 natural numbers.
questions.explanation: Average of first $n$ natural numbers = $\frac{n+1}{2} = \frac{26}{2} = 13$.

questions.question: 12 men can complete a project in 18 days. How many men are required to complete the same project in 8 days?
questions.explanation: $M_1 D_1 = M_2 D_2 \Rightarrow 12 \times 18 = M_2 \times 8 \Rightarrow M_2 = \frac{216}{8} = 27$ men.

questions.question: A car covers a journey at 40 km/h and returns along the same route at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the entire round trip?
questions.explanation: Average speed = $\frac{2xy}{x+y} = \frac{2 \times 40 \times 60}{40 + 60} = \frac{4800}{100} = 48\text{ km/h}$.

questions.question: If $x - \frac{1}{x} = 6$, find the value of $x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2}$.
The angles of a triangle are in the ratio $2 : 3 : 4$. What is the measure of the largest angle?
questions.explanation: Sum = $9x = 180^\circ \Rightarrow x = 20^\circ$. Largest angle = $4x = 80^\circ$.

questions.question: The circumference of a circle is $88\text{ cm}$. Taking $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$, find its area.
questions.explanation: $2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r = 88 \Rightarrow r = 14\text{ cm}$. Area = $\frac{22}{7} \times 14 \times 14 = 616\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.question: Find the total surface area of a cube whose volume is $343\text{ cm}^3$.
questions.explanation: Side $a = \sqrt[3]{343} = 7\text{ cm}$. Total Surface Area = $6a^2 = 6 \times 49 = 294\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.question: If $\sin\theta = \frac{5}{13}$ (where $\theta$ is acute), find the value of $\tan\theta$.
questions.explanation: Adjacent side = $\sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = 12$. Hence $\tan\theta = \frac{5}{12}$.

questions.question: A invests ₹40,000 for 12 months and B invests ₹60,000 for 8 months in a business. If total profit is ₹18,000, what is A's share?
An item marked at ₹1,200 is sold for ₹960 after a single discount. What is the discount percentage?
A 45-litre mixture of milk and water contains milk and water in the ratio $4 : 1$. How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio $3 : 2$?
questions.explanation: Milk = 36 L, Water = 9 L. For ratio $3:2$, water must be $\frac{2}{3} \times 36 = 24$ L. Added water = $24 - 9 = 15$ litres.

questions.question: Find the unit digit of $7^{53}$.
questions.explanation: Cyclicity of 7 is 4 (7, 9, 3, 1). $53 \bmod 4 = 1 \Rightarrow$ unit digit is $7^1 = 7$.

questions.question: What is the sum of all interior angles of a regular octagon (8-sided polygon)?
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles = $(n - 2) \times 180^\circ = 6 \times 180^\circ = 1080^\circ$.

questions.question: If $3x + 2y = 19$ and $x - y = 3$, find the value of $x + y$.
questions.explanation: From $x = y + 3$: $3(y+3) + 2y = 19 \Rightarrow 5y = 10 \Rightarrow y = 2, x = 5$. Thus $x + y = 7$.

questions.question: Find the value of $\cos 1^\circ \cdot \cos 2^\circ \cdot \cos 3^\circ \cdots \cos 180^\circ$.
questions.explanation: The product includes $\cos 90^\circ = 0$, making the entire product equal to 0.

questions.question: Two trains of lengths 140 m and 160 m run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h respectively. How long will they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = $(54+36) \times \frac{5}{18} = 25\text{ m/s}$. Total length = $140+160=300\text{ m}$. Time = $300/25 = 12$ s.

questions.question: Evaluate: $\sqrt{169} + \sqrt{289} - \sqrt{144}$

Marks scored by a student in 5 subjects (each out of 100):

| Subject | Marks |
|---|---|
| Maths | 88 |
| Physics | 76 |
| Chemistry | 84 |
| English | 72 |
| Computer | 90 |

What is the student's overall percentage?
questions.explanation: Total marks = $88 + 76 + 84 + 72 + 90 = 410$ out of 500. Percentage = $\frac{410}{500} \times 100 = 82\%$.

questions.question: In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, if $\angle A = 78^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle C$?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180^\circ$: $\angle C = 180^\circ - 78^\circ = 102^\circ$.

questions.question: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the seven-member Drafting Committee set up on 29 August 1947.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer ($23.5^\circ\text{ N}$) passes through how many Indian states?
questions.explanation: It passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.question: Kuchipudi is the classical dance form originating from which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Kuchipudi derives its name from Kuchipudi village in Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between the British East India Company and which Nawab of Bengal?
questions.explanation: Robert Clive's forces defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah on 23 June 1757 at Plassey.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure the purity (density) of milk?
questions.explanation: A Lactometer works on Archimedes' principle to measure the specific gravity/purity of milk.

questions.question: Which acid is naturally present in tamarind and grapes?
questions.explanation: Tartaric acid is found in tamarind and grapes (Oxalic in tomato/spinach, Formic in ant sting).

questions.question: Which blood group is universally known as the 'Universal Donor' for red blood cell transfusions?
questions.explanation: O-negative blood lacks A, B, and Rh(D) antigens on RBCs, making it the universal RBC donor.

questions.question: In India, who issues the one-rupee currency note and all coins?
options: Ministry of Finance, Government of India
questions.explanation: Under the Coinage Act, ₹1 notes (signed by the Finance Secretary) and coins are issued by the Ministry of Finance, while all other notes are issued by RBI.

questions.question: What is the minimum age required to contest elections for the Lok Sabha in India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 84, minimum age is 25 years for Lok Sabha and 30 years for Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Which is the largest brackish water lagoon in India?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake in Odisha is India's largest brackish water lagoon and Asia's largest coastal lagoon.

questions.question: The Great Bath, an iconic brick water tank of the Indus Valley Civilization, was excavated at which site?
questions.explanation: The Great Bath was discovered at Mohenjo-daro (Sindh, Pakistan) in the 1920s.

questions.question: In computing, what does `HTTP` stand for?
questions.explanation: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol, the foundation of web data communication.

questions.question: Which Indian city is home to the headquarters of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)?
questions.explanation: ISRO Headquarters (Antariksh Bhavan) is located in Bengaluru, Karnataka.

questions.question: Neeraj Chopra won India's first-ever Olympic athletics gold medal at Tokyo 2020 in which event?
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra won gold in Men's Javelin Throw with a throw of 87.58 m at Tokyo 2020 (held in 2021).

questions.question: Who gave the slogan 'Do or Die' during the launch of the Quit India Movement in August 1942?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi gave the clarion call 'Do or Die' at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay on 8 August 1942.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India?
questions.explanation: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act (2016) enabled the nationwide rollout of GST from 1 July 2017.

questions.question: Which hormone secreted by the pancreas regulates blood glucose levels by promoting cellular uptake of glucose?
questions.explanation: Beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete Insulin to lower blood sugar.

questions.question: Which Indian state shares the longest international land border with Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: West Bengal shares over 2,216 km of India's 4,096 km border with Bangladesh.

questions.question: The Sun Temple at Konark (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) was built in the 13th century by which ruler of the Eastern Ganga dynasty?
questions.explanation: King Narasimhadeva I constructed the Konark Sun Temple in Odisha around 1250 CE.

questions.question: Which metal remains in a liquid state at standard room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury (Hg, melting point $-38.8^\circ\text{C}$) is the only metal liquid at standard room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$).

questions.question: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission of India on which date?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) came into effect on 1 January 2015.

questions.question: The phenomenon responsible for the sparkling brilliance of a cut diamond and signal transmission in optical fibres is:
questions.explanation: Total Internal Reflection (TIR) occurs when light travels from a denser to a rarer medium above the critical angle.

questions.question: The Dronacharya Award is conferred annually by the Government of India for excellence in:
questions.explanation: Instituted in 1985, the Dronacharya Award honours outstanding coaches in sports and games.

questions.question: Who built the Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-e-Azam) stretching from Sonargaon in Bengal to Attock in the northwest?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri rebuilt and standardized the Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-e-Azam) and introduced the silver 'Rupiya'.

questions.question: Jim Corbett National Park, India's oldest national park (established 1936 as Hailey National Park), is situated in which state?
questions.explanation: Jim Corbett National Park lies in Nainital and Pauri Garhwal districts of Uttarakhand.
